description: Row identifier added when the partitioned files were created.
preprocessing: Dropped before modelling.
possible_security_meaning: Row index only. Carries no network semantics and is excluded as a predictor.

description: Record total duration
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Session length. Scans and floods are sub-second; exfiltration and C2 beacons persist.

description: Transaction protocol
preprocessing: Lower-cased and stripped; one-hot encoded with categories seen <200x in training folded into an 'infrequent' bucket.
possible_security_meaning: IP/transport protocol. Traffic on unusual protocols often indicates scanning or tunnelling.

description: http, ftp, smtp, ssh, dns, ftp-data ,irc and (-) if not much used service
preprocessing: Lower-cased and stripped; one-hot encoded with categories seen <200x in training folded into an 'infrequent' bucket.
possible_security_meaning: Application protocol identified by the analyser. '-' means unidentified, which is itself suspicious on a monitored network.

description: Indicates to the state and its dependent protocol, e.g. ACC, CLO, CON, ECO, ECR, FIN, INT, MAS, PAR, REQ, RST, TST, TXD, URH, URN, and (-) (if not used state)
preprocessing: Lower-cased and stripped; one-hot encoded with categories seen <200x in training folded into an 'infrequent' bucket.
possible_security_meaning: Connection outcome. INT (no reply) dominates scanning; FIN indicates a completed session.

description: Source to destination packet count
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Outbound packet count. High counts with tiny payloads indicate flooding.

description: Destination to source packet count
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Inbound packet count. Zero means the target never answered.

description: Source to destination transaction bytes
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Outbound volume. The primary signal for data exfiltration.

description: Destination to source transaction bytes
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Inbound volume. Large values with small requests can indicate amplification or bulk download.

description: Flow packet rate (packets/second). Present in the partitioned CSVs but absent from the authors' published feature list; derived from packet count and duration.
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Packets per second. Machine-generated attack traffic sustains rates a human session never reaches.

description: Source to destination time to live value
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Initial TTL from the source, a rough hop-count/OS fingerprint. In THIS dataset it is largely an artefact of the generator configuration - see the documented caveat.

description: Destination to source time to live value
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Initial TTL from the destination. Same artefact caveat as sttl.

description: Source bits per second
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Outbound bit rate. Sustained high values characterise denial-of-service traffic.

description: Destination bits per second
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Inbound bit rate. Near-zero alongside high sload means the target is not responding.

description: Source packets retransmitted or dropped
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Outbound packets lost or retransmitted. Elevated under congestion, which floods cause.

description: Destination packets retransmitted or dropped
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Inbound loss. A target shedding packets is a symptom of being overwhelmed.

description: Source interpacket arrival time (mSec)
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Outbound inter-packet gap. Very regular gaps suggest automation rather than a human.

description: Destination interpacket arrival time (mSec)
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Inbound inter-packet gap. Regularity can reveal beaconing malware.

description: Source jitter (mSec)
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Outbound jitter. Scripted traffic is unnaturally smooth; human traffic is bursty.

description: Destination jitter (mSec)
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Inbound jitter. Same reasoning applied to the responder.

description: Source TCP window advertisement value
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Advertised TCP receive window from the source. Zero implies the session never reached data transfer.

description: Source TCP base sequence number
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Source TCP base sequence number. Zero implies no established TCP session, as in a SYN scan.

description: Destination TCP base sequence number
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Destination TCP base sequence number. Zero implies the target never established the session.

description: Destination TCP window advertisement value
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Advertised TCP receive window from the destination. Zero implies no data-transfer state.

description: TCP connection setup round-trip time, the sum of synack and ackdat.
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: TCP handshake round-trip time. Zero means the three-way handshake never completed.

description: TCP connection setup time, the time between the SYN and the SYN_ACK packets.
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: SYN to SYN-ACK delay. Zero indicates a half-open connection - the SYN-scan signature.

description: TCP connection setup time, the time between the SYN_ACK and the ACK packets.
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: SYN-ACK to ACK delay. Zero means the client never completed the handshake.

description: Mean of the flow packet size transmitted by the src
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Mean outbound packet size. Small uniform packets indicate probing; large ones indicate payload delivery.

description: Mean of the flow packet size transmitted by the dst
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Mean inbound packet size. Zero when the target is silent.

description: Represents the pipelined depth into the connection of http request/response transaction
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: HTTP request/response pipeline depth. Unusual depths can indicate HTTP-based attacks.

description: Actual uncompressed content size of the data transferred from the servers http service.
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: HTTP response body size. Large values can indicate data being pulled out via HTTP.

description: No. of connections that contain the same service (14) and source address (1) in 100 connections according to the last time (26).
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Recent connections from this source to this service. High values indicate service enumeration.

description: No. for each state (6) according to specific range of values for source/destination time to live (10) (11).
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Authors' derived bucket over state and TTL. Inherits the TTL artefact and should be read with the same caution.

description: No. of connections of the same destination address (3) in 100 connections according to the last time (26).
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Recent connections to this destination. High values indicate a host being targeted.

description: No of connections of the same source address (1) and the destination port (4) in 100 connections according to the last time (26).
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Recent connections from this source to this destination port. A horizontal port-scan signal.

description: No of connections of the same destination address (3) and the source port (2) in 100 connections according to the last time (26).
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Recent connections to this destination from this source port. A vertical scan signal.

description: No of connections of the same source (1) and the destination (3) address in in 100 connections according to the last time (26).
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Recent connections between this exact host pair. Sustained pairing can indicate C2.

description: If the ftp session is accessed by user and password then 1 else 0.
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Whether the FTP session was authenticated. Documented as binary but is not - see defects.

description: No of flows that has a command in ftp session.
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Commands issued in the FTP session. Elevated counts accompany FTP brute-forcing.

description: No. of flows that has methods such as Get and Post in http service.
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Flows carrying HTTP GET/POST. Useful for separating web attacks from other HTTP traffic.

description: No. of connections of the same source address (1) in 100 connections according to the last time (26).
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Recent connections from this source overall. A noisy source is a scanning candidate.

description: No. of connections that contain the same service (14) and destination address (3) in 100 connections according to the last time (26).
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Recent connections to this service on this destination. Service-level targeting.

description: If source (1) and destination (3)IP addresses equal and port numbers (2)(4) equal then, this variable takes value 1 else 0
preprocessing: Passed through unscaled (already 0/1).
possible_security_meaning: Source and destination IP and port are identical - a spoofed or malformed packet (LAND-attack shape).

description: The name of each attack category. In this data set , nine categories e.g. Fuzzers, Analysis, Backdoors, DoS Exploits, Generic, Reconnaissance, Shellcode and Worms
role: Analysis only (EXCLUDED as predictor - target leakage)
preprocessing: Dropped before modelling.
possible_security_meaning: Attack family. ANALYSIS ONLY: it determines the target exactly, so using it as a predictor is target leakage.

description: 0 for normal and 1 for attack records
preprocessing: Dropped before modelling.
possible_security_meaning: The prediction target. 0 = benign, 1 = malicious.

description: Added by this project: which published file the record came from.
preprocessing: Dropped before modelling.
possible_security_meaning: Bookkeeping: which published file the record came from. Not a predictor.

description: Total bytes carried in both directions. Separates bulk transfers and data exfiltration from the tiny probe flows typical of scanning.
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Total bytes carried in both directions. Separates bulk transfers and data exfiltration from the tiny probe flows typical of scanning.

description: Total packets in both directions. A volume counterpart to byte count that is insensitive to payload size, so it isolates packet-rate attacks.
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Total packets in both directions. A volume counterpart to byte count that is insensitive to payload size, so it isolates packet-rate attacks.

description: Mean payload size across the whole flow. Floods and scans use minimal packets; exploit and shellcode deliveries push large payloads into few packets.
preprocessing: log1p transform, then standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Mean payload size across the whole flow. Floods and scans use minimal packets; exploit and shellcode deliveries push large payloads into few packets.

description: Share of flow bytes sent by the source, in [0, 1]. Values near 1.0 mean the source talked and the destination barely answered - the signature of scanning, spoofed floods and one-way probing. Values near 0 indicate a download-shaped flow.
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Share of flow bytes sent by the source, in [0, 1]. Values near 1.0 mean the source talked and the destination barely answered - the signature of scanning, spoofed floods and one-way probing. Values near 0 indicate a download-shaped flow.

description: Packet-count analogue of src_byte_ratio, in [0, 1]. Robust when payload sizes vary, e.g. reconnaissance that provokes variable-length errors.
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Packet-count analogue of src_byte_ratio, in [0, 1]. Robust when payload sizes vary, e.g. reconnaissance that provokes variable-length errors.

description: log1p(source bits/s) - log1p(destination bits/s). A signed, scale-stable measure of throughput asymmetry: strongly positive for outbound floods, strongly negative for large inbound responses.
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: log1p(source bits/s) - log1p(destination bits/s). A signed, scale-stable measure of throughput asymmetry: strongly positive for outbound floods, strongly negative for large inbound responses.

description: log1p(source jitter) - log1p(destination jitter). Machine-generated attack traffic is often unnaturally regular (low jitter) compared with human-driven sessions.
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: log1p(source jitter) - log1p(destination jitter). Machine-generated attack traffic is often unnaturally regular (low jitter) compared with human-driven sessions.

description: 1 when the destination returned no packets at all. The single clearest indicator of unanswered probing, closed-port scanning, or traffic sent to a spoofed or non-existent host.
preprocessing: Passed through unscaled (already 0/1).
possible_security_meaning: 1 when the destination returned no packets at all. The single clearest indicator of unanswered probing, closed-port scanning, or traffic sent to a spoofed or non-existent host.

description: 1 when both SYN-ACK and ACK-data round-trip times are non-zero, i.e. a full TCP three-way handshake completed. Half-open SYN scans and SYN floods deliberately never reach this state.
preprocessing: Passed through unscaled (already 0/1).
possible_security_meaning: 1 when both SYN-ACK and ACK-data round-trip times are non-zero, i.e. a full TCP three-way handshake completed. Half-open SYN scans and SYN floods deliberately never reach this state.

description: 1 when TCP base sequence numbers were observed in both directions, confirming a genuinely established bidirectional TCP session rather than a synthetic or aborted one.
preprocessing: Passed through unscaled (already 0/1).
possible_security_meaning: 1 when TCP base sequence numbers were observed in both directions, confirming a genuinely established bidirectional TCP session rather than a synthetic or aborted one.

description: 1 when both endpoints advertised a non-zero TCP receive window. Absence signals a connection that never reached a data-transfer state.
preprocessing: Passed through unscaled (already 0/1).
possible_security_meaning: 1 when both endpoints advertised a non-zero TCP receive window. Absence signals a connection that never reached a data-transfer state.

description: 1 when the flow's measured duration is exactly zero - a single-packet or sub-resolution event. Common for stateless UDP probes and for measurement artefacts that should be visible to the model rather than silently absorbed into a rate denominator.
preprocessing: Passed through unscaled (already 0/1).
possible_security_meaning: 1 when the flow's measured duration is exactly zero - a single-packet or sub-resolution event. Common for stateless UDP probes and for measurement artefacts that should be visible to the model rather than silently absorbed into a rate denominator.

description: 1 when the flow analyser could not identify an application-layer service. Traffic on non-standard ports that resists classification is operationally suspicious in its own right.
preprocessing: Passed through unscaled (already 0/1).
possible_security_meaning: 1 when the flow analyser could not identify an application-layer service. Traffic on non-standard ports that resists classification is operationally suspicious in its own right.

description: Fraction of source packets that were retransmitted or lost, in [0, 1]. Elevated loss accompanies congestion-inducing floods and unstable exploit payloads.
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Fraction of source packets that were retransmitted or lost, in [0, 1]. Elevated loss accompanies congestion-inducing floods and unstable exploit payloads.

description: Fraction of destination packets retransmitted or lost, in [0, 1]. Signals a target under strain - a denial-of-service symptom.
preprocessing: Standard-scaled (fitted on the training split only).
possible_security_meaning: Fraction of destination packets retransmitted or lost, in [0, 1]. Signals a target under strain - a denial-of-service symptom.
